title: Subquadratic Model Ties for First on Decision Index With 384k Context Window
summary:
The SubQ Snap 1.1 decision model uses Subquadratic Sparse Attention to reduce confident errors on unanswerable questions by 81%. Released by Subquadratic, the model tied for first place on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v1.0 with a score of 65, matching d1-ultra and Elephant 9B and beating Jev 1.14's score of 57. The model supports a 384k token context window in a single pass, significantly larger than the 32k window of d1-ultra and 16k of Elephant 9B, and scored 96.2 on When2Call benchmarks.

SubQ Snap 1.1 is priced at $0.04 per 1M input tokens with no charge for output, totaling about $30 per 1M tasks. This cost is similar to d1-ultra's $32 per 1M tasks, though Elephant 9B reaches the same 65 index score at $8.4 per 1M tasks. The model also achieved a 18% score on the HLE-MultiChoice subset of Humanity's Last Exam and a non-hallucination rate of 86%.

Today we're introducing the smartest, most capable version of our enterprise-ready decision model: SubQ Snap 1.1.

Snap is tied for #1 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index and has made big gains on agentic tasks, outperforming Jev by +7.2 points across 16 leading enterprise benchmarks.

All while maintaining 384k tokens of context, in a single pass, as the only model with constant compute per token.

- Powered by Subquadratic Sparse Attention.

- Tied for #1 on the @ArtificialAnlys Decision Index.

- 96.2 on When2Call, up from 75.2, and up 6 points on @huggingface 5 Tools & Automation benchmarks. It knows when to call a tool, when to ask, and when to decline.

- 81% fewer confident errors on questions it can't answer.

- $0.04 per 1M input tokens. No charge for output.

selectedTweets.text:
Subquadratic has released SubQ Snap 1.1, tying d1-ultra and Elephant 9B for first on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v1.0, driven by a low hallucination rate

SubQ Snap 1.1 is the new decision model from @subquadratic. It is priced at $0.04 per 1M input tokens and supports a 384K token context window, compared to 32K for d1-ultra and 16K for Elephant 9B.

Key takeaways:
➤ SubQ Snap 1.1 scores 65 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v1.0, tied with d1-ultra and Elephant 9B: the three models are 8 points ahead of the next model, Jev 1.14 (57).

➤ SubQ Snap 1.1's AA-Omniscience-Decision result is driven by a low hallucination rate: its non-hallucination rate of 86% is second only to Elephant 9B (93%), ahead of d1-ultra (85%). Its accuracy is 20%, compared to 32% for d1-ultra and 12% for Elephant 9B. The non-hallucination rate is the share of questions not answered correctly where the model chose "I don't know".

➤ SubQ Snap 1.1 scores 18% on HLE-MultiChoice: level with Elephant 9B (18%) and ahead of d1-ultra (15%). HLE-MultiChoice is the text-only multiple-choice subset of Humanity's Last Exam.

➤ SubQ Snap 1.1 costs $30 per 1M tasks: comparable to d1-ultra ($32), and ~3.6x the cost of Elephant 9B ($8.4), which scores the same 65.
